title: Valencia on sufficient grace
source_text: CXLIII. Ut vero aliquis censeatur habere sufficientem gratiam ad piam actionem, ex ejus sententia, necesse est ut habeat, aut omnia dona & auxilia, quae ad actionem tanquam illius principia, sive initia requiruntur, aut sic aliquod vel aliqua ex hujusmodi donis, ut per illud vel illa jam praeventus & excitatus, possit usu aliquo liberae facultatis suae, auxiliante Deo, acquirere reliqua omnia ejusmodi dona sive auxilia. Ut videre est apud jam dictum Gregorium tom. 2. disputat. 8. quaest. 3. punct. 4.
pass_a_gloss: CXLIII. But for someone to be judged to have sufficient grace for a pious action, in his opinion, it is necessary that he have, either all the gifts & aids, which are required for the action as its principles, or beginnings, or so some one or some of gifts of this kind, that through it or them already prevented & roused, he can by some use of his free faculty, God assisting, acquire all the rest of such gifts or aids. As may be seen in the aforesaid Gregory tom. 2. disputat. 8. quaest. 3. punct. 4.
pass_b_english: Thesis CXLIII. On his view, for someone to count as having sufficient grace for a devout action, he must have either all the gifts and aids that the action requires as its principles or starting points, or else one or more of those gifts, such that, forestalled and stirred by it or them, he can acquire all the remaining gifts or aids of that kind through some use of his free faculty, with God's help. This can be seen in Gregory, already named, tome 2, disputation 8, question 3, point 4.
